utterances.text: Hey, you doing okay there? What, what happened? You in some kind of trouble? Yeah. Why don't you let me help you out?
utterances.speaker: A
attribution_evidence: llm:Asks if B is doing okay, showing concern.

utterances.text: I, uh, I don't think that's a good idea.
utterances.speaker: B
attribution_evidence: llm:Expresses hesitance about A's offer for help.

utterances.text: Okay. Uh, well, I could call the police, so maybe they could get— No.
utterances.speaker: A
attribution_evidence: llm:Suggests calling the police as a solution.

utterances.text: No, do not do that, okay? Don't.
utterances.speaker: C
attribution_evidence: llm:Strongly opposes A's suggestion to call the police.

utterances.text: Okay. Well, look, I mean, if you need help, I could be that. Just get in the truck. I mean, who knows? You know, you'd probably even like it in there. It's freezing out here. It's a lot warmer in there. Trust me. Look, what kind of guy would I be to let a pretty girl in need just walk alone down this road? I mean, I should be driving, and I could, I could really use the company too.
utterances.speaker: A
attribution_evidence: llm:Offers help and assures warmth and safety.

utterances.text: Okay, I think it's best if you just get back in the car, okay?
utterances.speaker: B
attribution_evidence: llm:Advises A to return to the car, indicating authority.

utterances.text: No, just get in the truck. You need to— Easy. Relax. Relax, relax. We're going in. It's okay. You're okay. I'm okay. We're okay. Okay.
utterances.speaker: A
attribution_evidence: llm:Attempts to calm and reassure B while insisting on helping.
